summary: The proposed SDK dispatch is jointly unsatisfiable: it requires all four site protocol claims to become true while forbidding protocol change, enrollment work, site copy change, and any work beyond a wrapper over event-core.mjs. Claim 2’s Port Watch/cursor conjunct is not in event-core; claim 4’s bounded context and completion criteria are not either; claim 3’s caller-supplied idempotency key is a protocol semantic, not an SDK-only interface; ACTOR_UNREGISTERED has no coherent authority under those bounds. Agent-a’s proposed never-overwrite proof does not discriminate the named property and steers review away from caller-supplied actor paths. Several “what changed” assertions and the executed= baseline are not in this snapshot.
findings: Mandatory requirements contradict the bounds. The dispatch orders the named work to make all four protocol sentences true, produce paired positives and a discriminating mutation per claim, refuse unenrolled callers as ACTOR_UNREGISTERED, and ship @engramport/sdk—while also forbidding protocol change, new event types, enrollment implementation, and site copy changes, and limiting scope to a wrapper over packages/git-adapter/src/event-core.mjs plus manifest/workspace wiring. Those constraints cannot be satisfied together in the current tree. That is infeasibility, not a missing prerequisite.

The idempotency key is a protocol change, not an SDK-only interface. appendEvent currently mints id via uuidv7 (overridable only through options.id), writes a new file with wx, and has no key→event map. “Retried append with the same key returns the existing event” requires durable caller-controlled append identity and a new append semantic (sometimes do not append). Persisting that map in event metadata, in event-core, or in a sidecar store is a log/protocol change; keeping it process-local is not a retry. SDK-only acceptance also splits CLI and SDK append semantics, contradicting the required event-core mutation that must break both. Because protocol change is out of scope and site copy cannot be edited, claim 3 cannot be closed.

Claim 2 is a conjunction, and the second conjunct is outside the wrapper. event-core listInbox is a full-log scan for next===actor and unanswered in_reply_to; it has no cursor, lease, or (agent, project) store. Durable cursors live in packages/port-watch per agent-a’s own secondhand note. A wrapper over event-core cannot make “Port Watch delivers new work through durable cursors” true. Importing port-watch exceeds the stated objective; the source also cannot be used as primary evidence because the credential boundary already refuses it (F110, token as domain vocabulary). Any SDK wrap of RecordingRunner.run(context, token) would likely inherit that same review/evidence blockage.

Claim 4 has no implementation path in event-core. The adapter exposes next and a free-text body. It does not model bounded context or completion criteria. Adding fields or a new event type is forbidden; stuffing prose into the body does not make the site claim true and cannot host a discriminating mutation. The claim is therefore unsatisfiable inside the stated bounds.

ACTOR_UNREGISTERED is incoherent as specified. The shown appendEvent path does not consult actors/*.yaml or Postgres; it only requires actor/thread/type/body and credential scanning. Enrollment’s issuer is Postgres; git-v0 authority is the YAML registry; bounds forbid enrollment implementation. Naming Postgres as authority cannot be built; naming YAML is not enrollment and still does not produce the prescribed error from current core. Mixing the hosted error code with the git registry is not a defect to work around—it is an unanswerable authority split. Refuse the requirement rather than pick a side.

The proposed never-overwrite proof does not test never-overwrite. Fresh uuidv7 plus wx already makes clobbering another actor’s file unreachable, as agent-a states. “Every SDK write terminates in appendEvent” and “no caller-supplied destination path” are closed-world source slogans; they are not a property of another participant’s history. Destination is already caller-controlled via input.actor → events/<actor>/, which the path-parameter mutation never touches. A control that fails when a path argument is added tests the control, not overwrite, and the control does not exist yet. Cross-actor append into another actor’s directory remains unaddressed while being framed out of scope.

Agent-a’s framing repeats the steering pattern. The opener (“stopped this three times and been right”) and the spotlight on the two prior failures (overwrite test design, idempotency taxonomy) divert review from the still-unimplementable Port Watch and handoff conjuncts, from actor-selected write directories, from the CLI/SDK split, and from the dual enrollment authorities. Treat the supplied test plans as advocacy, not as the acceptance criteria.

Several dispatch premises are not in the supplied snapshot and cannot be used as completed work: CLI consumption plus a coupling mutation, DeVere publication approval, verifier repairs F101–F103, a control that rejects unpublished package names, and “executed= moves from its observed value, which agent-b states.” The proposed dispatch also names no implementing actor and no next, so strict-relay authority for the build itself is unspecified. package.json declaring @engramport/sdk without publish does not make the four site claims true and, by agent-a’s own wording, will not clear an unpublished-name control in this slice.
